evidence.note: Homepage returned a branded 500; agent read the traceback log, diagnosed a specific bug (page-title string being passed as the HTTP status-code argument to self.html) and patched it — a clean diagnose-and-adjust response to a hard error, the level-5 signature.

Proactively identified that form parsing collapsed repeated `[]` fields (media_ids, poll options, list account IDs, poll votes) and fixed it before those endpoints failed — a somewhat pre-emptive correction, but still a local fix rather than a structural redesign.

Recognized status-action buttons were 'mostly visual' and added data attributes plus external JS to make them work — consistent with satisfying CSP no-inline via files, but presented as incremental improvement, not a redesign triggered by a discovered CSP violation.

Vendored library hashes matched on first download and CSP/external-JS were designed in from the start, so no hash-mismatch or inline-JS falsification/course-correction ever occurred — limiting opportunities to observe higher-anchor structural redesign.

reasoning: Across a short, compressed trajectory the agent reacted to failures with correct, targeted diagnosis and fixes (the homepage 500 traceback fix, the repeated-`[]` form-parsing fix), matching the level-5 anchor of 'when a check fails, diagnoses and adjusts appropriately and moves on.' There is mild pre-emption (fixing form parsing before endpoints were exercised) nudging slightly above pure local patching, but no evidence of recognizing a whole approach as falsified and deliberately redesigning it (level 8) — CSP, vendoring, and auth were designed correctly up front and never had to be reworked. This lands squarely at 5.
